annotationRationale: Tangency determines nesting and disjointness. Circle-area differences then allow either exhaustive comparison or a universal upper bound with an attaining arrangement.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The maximum is 65π, choice D. Same-side disks are nested, while opposite-side interiors are disjoint. The statement, choices, and answer key are consistent; no figure is required.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful routes are supplied: complete enumeration and an upper bound with an attaining arrangement. Neither reference supplies another route that needs adding.
review.annotationCheck: Circle area and discrete extremal reasoning are appropriate assessed concepts. Tangent perpendicularity and relative circle positions correctly support the nesting argument.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Center distance R−r establishes same-side containment. Removing the second-largest disk leaves exactly-one coverage, regardless of smaller disks. Fixing radius 7 leaves exactly eight assignments. Their area coefficients are correctly computed as 24, 25, 33, 65, 32, 64, 64, and 65, proving the maximum.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE supplies nesting and an attaining arrangement; AoPS supplies the same arrangement without a complete maximum proof. The candidate adds independent exhaustive enumeration in original prose. Both references are correctly treated as third-party sources under source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The explanation justifies the geometry, the area rule, every table entry, and completeness of the cases. A learner can reconstruct the argument without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Both immediate IDs fit: cnm_p192 supplies the circular areas, and math:extremal-principle covers exhaustive comparison followed by an attaining configuration.

nativeLayerJudgments.US: The narrower 7.G.B.4 link supports circle-area use only. G-GMD.A.1 remains partial and does not establish formula-derivation coverage. Tangent support uses only the perpendicular-radius component of the narrower G-C.A.2 link.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The direct concepts match the written derivation. The local extremal node appropriately captures the finite placement problem; the supporting geometry IDs are also justified.

methodReviews.mathCheck: If 7 and 5 share a side, the contributions are at most 24π and 9π, totaling 33π. If separated, their disks cover 74π, but the entire radius-3 disk is excluded, giving at most 65π. Placing 7 alone opposite 5, 3, and 1 excludes no additional area beyond the radius-3 disk and attains 65π.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The sources support nesting and the attaining arrangement. The two-case universal bound is an independently developed completion, accurately labeled source-informed-original rather than an official MAA adaptation.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The first split is motivated by the largest disks. Both cases, the excluded-area bound, and equality are explained sufficiently for an AMC 10 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p192 directly supports the area estimates. math:extremal-principle precisely matches the universal bound and explicit construction attaining it.
